Feluda.description: A sharp, physically fit amateur detective and the story's protagonist.

Nilmoni Sanyal.description: A wealthy, eccentric collector of antiques who claims to be the victim of mysterious threats and a burglary.

Pratul Datta.description: A retired lawyer and rival collector who competes with Nilmoni Sanyal at auctions.

Jhuntu.description: Supposedly Nilmoni Sanyal's nephew, later revealed to be a beggar boy involved in the plot.

Nandalal.description: One of Nilmoni Sanyal's old and trusted servants.

Panchu.description: Another of Nilmoni Sanyal's old and trusted servants.

Bangshalochan.description: Pratul Datta's servant who is attacked during the burglary.

Dr Bose.description: A doctor called to attend to Jhuntu when he is unwell.

sheershasan.description: A yoga posture where one stands on the head, considered beneficial for health.

Puja.description: A Hindu religious festival or ritual, often involving holidays and family gatherings.

Jamshedpur.description: An industrial city in eastern India, mentioned as the place where Baba is on tour.

All India Rifle Competition.description: A national-level shooting competition in India.

Roland Road.description: A street in Calcutta (Kolkata), where Nilmoni Sanyal lives.

Rangers Lottery.description: A lottery mentioned as the source of Nilmoni Sanyal's wealth.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, a major city in eastern India where the story is set.

Aratoon Brothers.description: An auction house in Calcutta where antiques are bought and sold.

Elgin Road.description: A locality in Calcutta, referenced as a postmark on the mysterious envelopes.

Japan.description: A country in East Asia, mentioned as the place where Jhuntu's parents are.

Free School Street.description: A street in Calcutta known for shops and auction houses.

Lovelock Street.description: A street in Calcutta, address of Pratul Datta.

Naktola.description: A locality in Calcutta, used as a false address by Feluda during a phone call.

Joynarayan Bagchi.description: A pseudonym used by Feluda while investigating Pratul Datta.

Subodh.description: A pseudonym used by Topshe during the investigation.

Shyamasangeet.description: Devotional songs dedicated to the Hindu goddess Kali, popular in Bengal.

khanjani.description: A small hand-held percussion instrument, similar to a tambourine, used in folk music.

Ambassador.description: A classic Indian car model, widely used as taxis and private vehicles.

Ma.description: Bengali/Hindi for 'mother', used both literally and as a respectful form of address.

yoga.description: A traditional Indian discipline involving physical postures, breathing, and meditation.

chick-peas.description: Also known as chana, a legume commonly eaten in India.

Baba.description: A respectful term for father in Bengali and other Indian languages.

goonda.description: A Hindi term for a thug or hired muscle.

paan.description: A preparation of betel leaf with areca nut and sometimes tobacco, chewed for its stimulant effects.

kurta.description: A traditional loose-fitting shirt worn in South Asia.

pyjamas.description: Loose trousers, often part of traditional Indian sleepwear.

Babu.description: A respectful or polite form of address for a man in Bengali and Hindi.

dal.description: A dish made from lentils, a staple in Indian cuisine.

chutney.description: A condiment in Indian cuisine made from fruits, vegetables, and spices.

dahi.description: Curd or yogurt in Hindi and Bengali.

namaskar.description: A traditional Indian greeting, similar to 'namaste', involving folded hands.

siesta.description: An afternoon nap, a word of Spanish origin but commonly used in India.

cheroot.description: A type of cigar, often associated with South Asian and colonial contexts.
